answer: Agents such as sparrow, ember, and onyx must each lock a refundable bond before receiving unsecured trade credit, with credit capped below the bond’s value. If an agent defaults, a verifiable unpaid invoice triggers seizure of its bond to repay the seller. Creating more identities therefore creates no cheap borrowing power: an attacker must immobilize fresh capital for every alias and loses more collateral than it can steal through default.
